# Results (generated by ml/write_results_md.py from results/metrics.json — do not edit by hand)

## What the phone runs
- Frozen MobileNetV3-Large image backbone (ImageNet weights, Apache-2.0): **16.8 MB** ONNX, ~4 ms per photo on a laptop CPU (phone speed not yet measured).
- Small head: **68 KB** JSON. Familiarity reference (1,000 stored training photos as int8 vectors): **1284 KB**.
- The ONNX path reproduces the Python pipeline: 25/25 same class, max embedding difference 0.0001.

## Data
- Training: 7045 photos — 1,500 sampled per class from JMuBEN/JMuBEN2 (Kenya, Kirinyaga, arabica; 58,550 images, many are rotated/flipped copies) plus half of the BRACOL photos we could recover (Brazil, arabica; Mendeley archive is truncated, 1,342 usable of 1,747).
- Calibration (temperature, threshold, familiarity cutoff): the other half of BRACOL (672 photos).
- Sealed field test: RoCoLe (Ecuador, robusta, on-plant smartphone photos) — 1385 healthy/rust photos; 167 red-spider-mite photos as an out-of-scope test.

## Findings
1. **Lab accuracy does not transfer to the field.** On held-out lab-style photos the model is right 84% of the time. On field photos it is right 2.5% of the time, while reporting 93% average confidence. A tool that trusted its own confidence would give confident wrong answers.
2. **The familiarity check catches this.** Comparing each photo with the 1,000 stored training photos separates field photos from lab photos almost perfectly (AUROC 0.999; model confidence alone scores 0.29, worse than chance). Out of the box the tool says "not sure — the officer will look" to **99.6%** of field photos and **100%** of photos of a pest it was never trained on.
3. **The learning loop localises the model.** When the officer labels field photos, the head is refit on the phone (pulled toward the lab model) and the labelled photos join the familiarity reference:

| Officer labels | Photos answered | Answers correct | Answers correct, local labels only (no lab model) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0% | 0% | 0% |
| 10 | 61% | 74% | 63% |
| 20 | 82% | 75% | 69% |
| 50 | 91% | 82% | 80% |
| 100 | 94% | 85% | 84% |
| 200 | 96% | 86% | 85% |

   Starting from the lab model matters most when labels are few (74% vs 63% correct at 10 labels). An update to share with other phones is ~13 KB for the head plus 1284 bytes per labelled photo.
4. **Co-op early warning (simulation, synthetic villages).** Using the error rates measured after 50 officer labels, across 40 villages per round with about 6.5 real outbreaks: raw shares raise 8.1 false alarms and miss 1.2 outbreaks per round; small-sample-adjusted shares (alert when the chance that the share is above 25% exceeds 0.5 — the same rule the app uses) raise 4.7 false alarms and miss 2.0. If the officer can visit 5 villages, the adjusted ranking sends them to 3.3 real outbreaks vs 3.0 for raw shares. The adjustment trades fewer false alarms for more misses; villages below the alert line still appear in the ranked list.
5. **Size vs accuracy.** A 5x larger backbone (DINOv2-small, 21.6M parameters, ~87 MB) is right 49% of the time on field photos with no local labels (vs 2.5%); after 50 labels it answers 58% of photos with 90% correct. We ship the small model to respect the side-loading constraint.
6. **Limit found: unknown pests after adaptation.** Before local labels the tool says "not sure" to 100% of red-spider-mite photos (a pest it was never taught). After 50 officer labels it says "not sure" to only 22%; of the rest, 81 are flagged as rust (the officer still hears about a problem) and 45 are wrongly called healthy. Mitigations in the app: a "different problem / not in list" label for the officer, and a spot-check that queues 1 in 10 answered photos for the officer anyway.

## Simplifications (stated)
- JMuBEN contains augmented copies of the same leaf; its in-domain validation score (100%) is optimistic and not used as a headline.
- No training or test photo comes from Kenyan farms in field conditions; the field test is Ecuadorian robusta. Leaf rust looks similar across species, but this is a proxy.
- Learning-loop labelled photos and test photos both come from RoCoLe (one region, one photographer), so adaptation is easier here than across real farms.
- The village simulation uses synthetic villages; only the classifier error rates are measured.
- Labels in the learning loop come from the dataset authors, standing in for an extension officer.
